title: Selection Boundaries for Influence-Ranked External-Control Borrowing
banked_reason: The delivered result is a specialized warning rather than a field-tier inference contribution; the selected law, sharp modulus, and computable uniformly valid interval remain open.
gap_reasons: The delivered result is a specialized warning rather than a field-tier inference contribution.
It does not determine the sharp modulus beyond the lower statement omega*(0)>0, establish any law for the selected estimator, or construct a computable uniformly valid interval.
The delivered core supplies only separate negative witnesses and a conditional transfer while expressly leaving the interval, coverage, length, and selected law open.
Pointwise smooth score fitting, scalar score density, and Holder boundary moments do not imply differentiability of the fitted-score sublevel-set integral.
proof_attempt_summary: The run repaired and verified two separate anchor-relevant obstructions: a non-Gaussian generated-rank boundary term and an exact leading-risk tie with separated root-n ATE coordinates. A bounded positive-theory attempt isolated the missing fitted-score sublevel-set differentiability primitive; without it, the uniform all-prefix expansion and localization argument could not be derived. The sharp modulus, selected-estimator law, and computable tie-uniform interval therefore remain open, leaving a sound incremental warning below the field floor.
tldr: Influence-ranked external-control borrowing has two verified necessity boundaries inside the displayed Yang--Li--Wu--Yang sample architecture.  A continuous generated ranking can create a quantitatively nondegenerate, non-Gaussian fixed-cardinality boundary term, so the frozen \(\Gamma_n\)-Gaussian all-prefix coupling and every covariance-only repair fail.  Separately, exact leading-risk ties can retain nonvanishing root-\(n\) ATE-coordinate distance, including between two positive prefixes; the repaired finite-support witness also defines the external potential outcomes on every row.  No Yang theorem asserts the refuted coupling.  A bounded feasibility attempt on a smooth-localizable generated-prefix subclass fails at the primitive fitted-score sublevel-set derivative, so the corrected selected law, sharp observable modulus, and computable tie-uniform interval remain unresolved and the present negative-plus-conditional package does not meet the positive Stat field-tier inference floor.
gap: Yang, Li, Wu, and Yang's Theorem~2 controls one given prefix, whereas their Theorem~3 selects a random prefix on a generated ranking; neither theorem supplies uniform expansion, the local quadratic argmin law, or post-selection ATE coverage at multiple minima. Patel, DiTraglia, Zuber, and Burgess settle analogous focused-selection inference for a fixed invalid-instrument problem but not for generated individual ranks or a growing nested causal path.
fill: The project supplies the fixed-stratum all-prefix expansion and quadratic local law, establishes a legal tied-risk counterexample, and uses the resulting selection geometry to formulate nominal tie-uniform multiplier inference.
